steps.thought: List the available station tests to see the available options and their costs.

tests.name: power_on_selftest
tests.description: Boot the unit and enumerate devices on I2C, UART and CAN.

tests.name: battery_rest_check
tests.description: Read pack and per-cell voltages at rest.

tests.name: esc_telemetry
tests.description: Read ESC telemetry: sync errors, packet loss, back-EMF detection.

tests.name: compass_static
tests.description: Compare compass heading to the fixture reference with motors off.

tests.name: harness_continuity
tests.description: Measure per-bus continuity resistance and CAN termination.

tests.name: camera_selftest
tests.description: Run camera built-in self test and measure frame rate and CSI errors.

tests.name: imu_static
tests.description: Log 1000 IMU samples on the static fixture: gyro bias, accel noise, dropouts.

tests.name: motor_spin_test
tests.description: Spin all motors at 50 percent throttle: current, RPM, RPM jitter, temp.

tests.name: compass_motor_interference
tests.description: Sweep throttle 0-75 percent and log compass heading deviation.

tests.name: battery_load_test
tests.description: Apply a 20 A load and measure sag, cell imbalance, internal resistance.

steps.thought: I will run power_on_selftest as the cheapest initial system check to enumerate all core devices on I2C, UART, and CAN buses.
steps.observation: The power-on self test failed because the I2C devices 'imu' and 'compass' were not found, while CAN nodes and camera_ctrl over UART were successfully enumerated.

hypotheses.rationale: Both I2C-based devices (imu and compass) failed to enumerate, strongly pointing to a loose or disconnected I2C harness connector.
Could be an IMU power or hardware failure causing it to drop off I2C, but less likely to simultaneously affect the compass.
Compass missing on I2C could be due to a localized sensor failure, though connector is more probable.

steps.thought: I will run the harness_continuity test to check the resistance and connections of the I2C bus harness, which is the cheapest and most direct way to confirm whether the connector is loose or damaged.
steps.observation: The harness continuity test revealed that the I2C bus continuity is intermittent with a resistance of 3.54 ohms, which directly explains why both the IMU and compass I2C devices were not found during the power-on selftest.

hypotheses.rationale: Intermittent I2C bus continuity and missing I2C devices (IMU and compass) strongly indicate a loose I2C connector.
An internal IMU failure could theoretically cause the bus issue, but the missing compass points more universally to a shared I2C connection fault.

steps.thought: The I2C connector is loose, causing intermittent continuity and preventing the IMU and compass from being found. I will now propose the rework to reseat the I2C connector without needing any further tests.
steps.observation: Rework applied; full suite passed: True.
